correctness.rationale: For every \(D,r,\kappa,L,Q>0\), the explicit Robin profile solves \(-Dc^{\prime\prime}+rc=Q\delta_{L/2}\) in distributions with the correct endpoint fluxes and central jump; strict energy coercivity gives uniqueness. The inequalities \(\sinh a>a\), \(\cosh a>1\) and \(a\cosh a>\sinh a\) establish \(1<B<F(L/2)\). Strict increase of \(F\) yields exactly two crossings. Exact integration proves the strict height-mean inequality. The Robin semigroup proves the qualified long-time dose ordering, not short-time ordering. The standalone finite checker independently passed the elementary case and 504 illustrative positive configurations.

originality.rationale: The authorial contribution is the exact all-parameter comparison of a centrally emitted Robin-deposition slab with a surface-to-volume-matched global-sink comparator, including exactly two crossover heights and an opposite strict height-mean bias. Full relevant primary text was inspected; earlier ventilator comparisons already allow generic spatial sign reversal, so only the precise Robin deposition classification is asserted. Unknown unindexed textbook equivalents remain a residual risk.
residual_risks: A standard Green-function textbook or unindexed older indoor dispersion source may already have stated the same calibrated comparison and sharp crossing law.
A laterally uniform emitting plane is not a realistic single-person emission distribution and makes the exact classification much easier than real three-dimensional geometry.
The initiating simulation uses a removal-rate convention not assumed numerically identical to the surface-to-volume calibration; no empirical claims transfer automatically.

value.rationale: Recent airborne infection risk models directly compare global uniform aerosol removal and local surface deposition. The minimal exact result gives a parameter-independent conservatism map: a calibrated global sink overpredicts adjacent to depositing walls, underpredicts a central exposure region and the spatial mean, with explicit threshold for receiver altitude and eventual fixed-receiver cumulative dose. This answers a genuinely motivated modelling-interpretation gap, not merely a known Green function evaluation or arbitrary parameter table. The result is only an idealized benchmark and has no direct empirical validation.
